reader.requirement: At 85, identifier-1 and identifier-3 through identifier-7 are inspected as character strings. Alphabetic and alphanumeric items are taken as they are (3a). Alphanumeric edited, numeric edited and unsigned numeric items are taken as if redefined alphanumeric (3b). A signed numeric item is taken as if moved to an unsigned item of its length excluding a separate sign (3c), and a signed identifier-1 keeps its original sign after the statement. This holds in every format.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.InspectBeforeFromFirstEligiblePosition (from 2023): at 85 a BEFORE delimiter is located from the leftmost position (BoundInspect.BeforeFromLeftmost = true), at 2023 from the first eligible position

DialectBehavior.InspectFormat3LengthIdentifiedOnce (from 2002): a format 3 over an occurs-depending identifier-1 at 85 sets ReplacingTakesLengthAnew (InspectEmitter#EmitBody re-reads identifier-1 for the REPLACING half); from 2002 the DEPENDING ON object is frozen

reader.edition-search: The GR3 members (OperandText.AsItemCharacters with deSign: true, InspectEmitter.EmitStore, CobolNum.RetainSign, UsageCollectionPass, StorageFormPass) carry no edition reference (grep 'Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior|IsActive' over those files: none). The path's only edition consults are the two InspectBinder switches listed, and neither touches the class treatment.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: gr3.cob prints identically at --std 85 and --std 2023. (At 85 a numeric literal VALUE on a numeric-edited item is refused with COBOL0900, a different rule, so the probe uses a nonnumeric VALUE.)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1128_inspect_signed_sign_retained covers 3c sign retention for identifier-1 in format 2 (separate leading/trailing and overpunch). It does not exercise 3c for identifier-3/4/5 operands, the separate sign excluded from TALLYING, 3b edited and unsigned numeric items, format 4 on signed items, the 18-digit item, or reference modification (probed below).

probes.printed: R15=[129-] (S2(1:3) REPLACING ALL "3" BY "9" over a TRAILING SEPARATE item)
probes.expected: the reference-modified item is alphanumeric (3a): digits replaced, the separate sign position outside the reference untouched

probes.printed: T2=00,03 (TALLYING FOR ALL "-" and FOR CHARACTERS over S9(3) SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE VALUE -123)
probes.expected: 3c: the length excludes the separate sign position, so no "-" and 3 characters

probes.printed: T1=01 (overpunched -123 FOR ALL "3"); T3=01 (pattern S9 VALUE -3 reads "3"); T4=00 (BEFORE a LEADING SEPARATE -1 reads "1"); T5=02 and R5=[  1,50] (numeric edited); R6=[xyCD ] (alphanumeric edited); R7=[X12X] (unsigned 9(4)); R8=[ABZA] (alphabetic); R9=[-125] (CONVERTING a LEADING SEPARATE -120); R13=[005-] and R14=[335-] (signed pattern and replacement read without sign)
probes.expected: 3a/3b/3c: signed operands inspected without their sign, edited and unsigned items as their character image, a signed identifier-1 keeps its sign

probes.printed: R10=[-111111111111111111], then ADD 1 gives [-111111111111111110] (S9(18), the 85 maximum); R11=[+777] (zero, positive sign kept); R12=[-000] (-100 REPLACING ALL "1" BY "0": negative zero kept)
probes.expected: 3c: the original sign is retained, a zero result included

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR3c  (6.18.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3c
OK  §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR3b  (6.18.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3b

reader.notes: Every class of item GR3 names was probed, as identifier-1 and as an operand, in formats 1, 2 and 4. All printed what 3a-3c prescribe, including the excluded separate sign and the retained negative zero. The class treatment is edition-invariant code, which fits a rule that does not change between editions.

refuter.evidence: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-016/ri3b.cob at --std 85: G1 group holding S9(2) TRAILING SEPARATE -12 TALLYING FOR ALL "-" -> 01 (a group is alphanumeric, 3a: its sign is a character); G2 S999 SIGN LEADING (overpunch) -123 REPLACING ALL "1" BY "7" -> -723 (leading overpunched digit read and the sign retained, 3c); G3 -> 01; G4 signed identifier-6 (S9 -2) as from-set -> 1Z34; G5 signed identifier-7 (S9 -8) as to-set -> 8234; G6 numeric edited identifier-7 (Z9 = " 5") -> " 534" (3b); G8/G9 S9(3) LEADING SEPARATE -101: CHARACTERS -> 03, CONVERTING "01" TO "98" -> -898 (sign kept); G10/G11 9PP and S9PP: CHARACTERS -> 01 (the item's character positions, not its scaled digits); G12 S9PP -200 REPLACING "2" BY "3" -> -300; G13 9V99 FOR ALL "." CHARACTERS -> 03; G14/G15 S9(18) LEADING SEPARATE (85's largest): REPLACING -> -923456789092345678 (both 1s, sign kept), CHARACTERS -> 18; G16 alphanumeric-edited XBX as identifier-3 -> 1ZZZ. All per 3a-3c; 2023 prints the same. A side finding, not a GR3 defect: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-016/ri3.cob with REPLACING ALL "1" BY L5 (S9 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE) is refused at 85 with COBOL0846 citing SR7 (L5 is 2 characters); SR7 measures the data item's size, which counts a separate sign, so the refusal follows SR7's text (§1985:VI.6.18.3 SR7: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.18.3 SR7  (6.18.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR7'); 2023 accepts it. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR3c  (6.18.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3c'.
